newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian lottery farce heads for happy ending.
newsitem.headline: Italian lottery farce heads for happy ending.

text.p: An enquiry into a foul-up that turned Italy's richest lottery into a fiasco recommended on Thursday that a punter's contested $1.3 million win should stand and that the state should pay four other people damages.

Popular faith in the efficiency of the state, minimal at the best of times, took a knock on January 6 when television viewers watching the live draw saw four out of 10 numbered balls get stuck in one of the machines used to select the winning tickets.
Organisers pressed on regardless after failing to dislodge the balls with a primitive shove and announced that ticket U-527423 had won a two billion lire ($1.3 million) bonanza.

The joy of the lucky punter, who has yet to come forward, lasted less than 24 hours before organisers annulled the win and awarded it to the holder of a ticket that had won just 200 million lire ($130,000).
The enquiry, conducted by three magistrates, was ordered by Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco amid public outrage and a rash of jokes about the state's inability to get anything right.
It found that the draw had been mismanaged and recommended that the original winner should have the prize restored.

It also recommended consolation prizes of 200 million lire to the holders of tickets which ended with the numbers on the four balls that got jammed. It recommended restoring the substitute winner's lesser prize.
The findings were welcomed by consumer groups but the biggest sigh of relief came from Visco, who said he hoped the lottery organisers would accept the recommendations forthwith.
"The situation that arose went beyond the...lottery and has risked doing serious damage to the credibility of the state in the eyes of the public," Visco said in a statement.
